definitions.explanation: One of several causes or contributing factors. Implies that the cause mentioned is not the only one, but one among multiple factors.

examples.japanese: ⟦ストレス→ストレス：03827_sutoresu⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{病気|びょうき}→病気：00771_byouki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一因|いちいん}だ。
examples.english: Stress is also a contributing factor to illness.

examples.japanese: ⟦{人手|ひとで}{不足|ぶそく}→人手不足：11436_hitodebusoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{事故|じこ}→事故：00851_jiko⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一因|いちいん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: A shortage of workers was one cause of the accident.

examples.japanese: ⟦{食生活|しょくせいかつ}→食生活：21071_shokuseikatsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{乱|みだ}れ→乱れ：11413_midare⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生活習慣病|せいかつしゅうかんびょう}→生活習慣病：08620_seikatsushuukanbyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一因|いちいん}になっている⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: Poor eating habits are said to be a contributing factor to lifestyle diseases.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一因|いちいん}だ: is a contributing factor of ~
- ～⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一因|いちいん}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: become a contributing factor of ~
- ～⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{一因|いちいん}になっている: is one of the factors behind ~

USAGE:
Using {一因|いちいん} implies the speaker acknowledges multiple causes. It is more measured than ⟦{原因|げんいん}→原因：01400_genin⟧ (cause), which can imply a single or primary cause.

REGISTER:
A somewhat formal word, common in news, academic writing, and analysis.
